summary: src/types.ts is a clean, thorough type definition module. All 7 exported types/interfaces match the spec. JSDoc is accurate and complete. No blocking issues found. No fix-forward changes applied.

Four observations recorded (all low-priority): (1) PreflightCheck is sync-only while Command.run is async-capable — this asymmetry is defensible (preflight checks throw synchronously per design) but worth revisiting if async preflight I/O is ever needed. (2) SetupComponent methods (run/detect/validate) are all synchronous — consistent with each other, though the same async extension concern applies if shell commands are needed. (3) Command.key is typed string | null with no single-character enforcement at the type level — TypeScript limitation, correctly documented in JSDoc. (4) NodeJS.ProcessEnv reference in ScriptRunnerOptions confirmed safe via @types/node in devDependencies.

comments.note: PreflightCheck = () => void is sync-only. Command.run is () => void | Promise<void> for contrast. If async preflight I/O is ever required (port checks, service pings), this alias will need updating to () => void | Promise<void>. Acceptable deferred decision — sync-throw semantics are correct for Phase A.

SetupComponent.run/detect/validate are all synchronous (boolean returns). Consistent with each other but the same async extension concern as PreflightCheck applies. If these methods need to shell out, the return types would need Promise<boolean>.

Command.key: string | null does not enforce single-character length at the type level — TypeScript limitation. JSDoc correctly documents the intent ('Single-character key'). Runtime validation in createMenu() should enforce this constraint when it is implemented.
No observations — code in src/types.ts is clean, idiomatic, and consistent. JSDoc is thorough and accurate across all seven exports.
